title: Mysterium Cosmographicum (Latin, 1596)
author: Johannes Kepler
description: Mysterium Cosmographicum (The Cosmographic Mystery), Johannes Kepler's first major work, published in Latin at Tübingen in 1596. A passionate defence of the Copernican heliocentric system, it proposes that the number, distances and order of the six then-known planets are explained by nesting the five Platonic solids (cube, tetrahedron, dodecahedron, icosahedron and octahedron) between the planetary spheres, a design Kepler believed revealed the geometric plan by which God created the universe. He also suggests that a force emanating from the Sun moves the planets, the seed of physical astronomy, and compares his model with observational data. The theory was later superseded, but the book launched Kepler's career, brought him to the attention of Tycho Brahe and Galileo, and shows the fusion of Pythagorean sacred geometry, theology and empirical science at the birth of modern astronomy.
